page.layout: Running head at top centre with page number 160 at top left. Main text in one block of full-width lines. Left margin notes: "Dall. pag. 295." beside the first lines, and "Pearf. pag. 30." beside the last lines. Catchword "tinum," at the right below the last line.

main_text.l: Dallæi conjecturæ locum dedit; conjec-
turam autem suam suffultam volebat,
primùm mirifico quodam Petavii effugio,
quo illa de Sige verba à Valentini sensu
abducere conatus est. Quid ad hæc Vir
doctus; dicit Dallæum aliter atque aliter
de Petavio sentire; quasi verò crimen sit
de celeberrimo illo Iesuita ita sentire;
dùm vera narrat ac sequitur, à Dallæo
probatur, dum falsa scribit rejicitur:
nihil aliud hoc in loco sibi vult Dallæus,
nisi Petavium verba de quibus controver-
titur, Valentinum notare vidisse, & ea
propter plura ex[illegible, ~2 letters]gitasse, ut illa à Va-
lentini sensu abduceret; secundò asserit
ibidem Dallæus verba ista ad Valentini
dogma adeò apta atque apposita esse, ut
etiamsi mens auctoris aliò, dùm ea scri-
beret, respexisset: fieri tamen non po-
tuerit, quin ea Irenæus si nosset, arripe-
ret, & contra Valentini expositum à se
somnium alicubi usurparet; cui scilicet
adeò bellè congruunt, ut in id ipsum pri-
mò ab Auctore destinata non possint non
videri, si totam orationem simpliciter, &
absque ullo præjudicio legeris: constat
tamen Irenæum nusquam in totâ contra
Valentinianos disputatione, horum ver-
borum meminisse. Respondet Pearsonius
non ita disputasse Salmasium, non Albertinum,

page.notes: Printed page number 160 and running head "Observationes in Posteriorem" at top. The word "excogitasse" is covered by an ink blot; the letters under it are not legible, so the gap is marked. "abduceret" is partly covered by the same blot and is read from the visible letters with the blot in the way (possibly "abduceret"). The catchword "tinum," is the continuation of "Albertinum," on the next page.
